11.about: A relentless perpetuum mobile in D minor: repeated notes, chromatic figures and crossing hands build into a hammering, machine-like drive that dispenses with conventional themes. It is one of the most exciting virtuoso showpieces of the twentieth century.
11.ctx: Written while Prokofiev was a student at the St Petersburg Conservatory. Its percussive style shocked critics, but his friend Nikolai Myaskovsky praised it as clever, edgy and full of personality. It follows in the line of Schumann’s Toccata, Op. 7.
facts: A classic of the ‘percussive’ modern piano style.

22.about: Twenty miniatures, most lasting under a minute, ranging from delicate lyricism to grotesque humour and violent outbursts. The title comes from a poem by Konstantin Balmont about seeing whole worlds in every fleeting vision.
22.ctx: Composed in clusters between 1915 and 1917, just before the Russian Revolution drove Prokofiev abroad. Some pieces were inspired by people close to him, and he said No. 19 was inspired by the events of February 1917 in Petrograd. Being technically not too demanding, they are much used in teaching.
parts: Calm, bell-like opening in the high register.
No. 19: Presto agitatissimo e molto accentuato
Violent and driving; inspired, Prokofiev said, by the February 1917 revolution.
facts: The title comes from a poem by Konstantin Balmont.
Henle rates the pieces at levels 3–6.

75.about: Ten pieces arranged by Prokofiev himself from his ballet ‘Romeo and Juliet’, from lively dances and character portraits to the famous ‘Montagues and Capulets’ and the lovers’ farewell. The piano writing ranges from delicate cantilenas to massive cascades of chords.
75.ctx: Prokofiev compiled the piano set, like two orchestral suites, before the ballet itself reached the stage — its premiere took place in Brno in 1938. Henle’s is the first Urtext edition of the set.
parts: The arrival of guests at the Capulets’ ball.
A portrait of the playful young Juliet.
Romeo and his friends arrive masked at the ball.
The famous ‘Dance of the Knights’, heavy and menacing.
A calm, kindly portrait of the friar.
A witty, mercurial portrait of Romeo’s friend.
No. 9: Dance of the Girls from the Antilles
No. 10: Romeo and Juliet Before Parting
The lovers’ farewell, the lyrical climax of the set.
facts: Arranged by Prokofiev from his own ballet.
The ballet premiered in Brno in 1938.
Henle rates the pieces at levels 4–7.

83.about: The shortest and most famous of Prokofiev’s three ‘war sonatas’. A nervous, dissonant first movement marked Allegro inquieto gives way to a warm, singing Andante caloroso, and the sonata ends with the celebrated Precipitato, a relentless toccata in 7/8 time.
83.ctx: Composed during the Second World War. Sviatoslav Richter gave the premiere, having reportedly learned it in just four days. The sonata won a Stalin Prize in 1943.
parts: A restless, dissonant movement with a slower, uneasy central section.
A warm, lyrical melody that builds to an anguished climax.
A thundering toccata in 7/8, one of the most famous finales of the century.
